items.title: AI data center power demand will double by 2030 thanks to $4 trillion in spending, adding an entire Great Britain to energy strain
items.description: IEA's report says that power production and distribution is barely keeping up with the rapid growth of AI data centers.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Instagram Share this article 3 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter The AI data center build-out is pushing electricity grids across the globe, with many regions facing demand from projects that would exceed the current peak load that each system could support. According to the International Energy Agency’s (IEA) World Energy Outlook 2026 report, a total of 120GW of capacity is currently available across all types of data centers across the globe, with another 120GW expected to be completed by the end of the decade, 75% of which would be dedicated to artificial intelligence. Aside from that, it’s also tracking 93 large “AI factories” that are either under construction or being expanded via satellite imagery. It estimates that the capacity for these sites grew from under 2GW to 17GW in just two years, and that they’re expected to hit a total of 50GW upon completion, the equivalent of adding a second Great Britain to power demand.Go deeper with TH Premium: AI and data centers (Image credit: Microsoft)The data center cooling state of playThe custom AI ASIC state of play America’s AI chip rules keep changing — and the rest of the world is paying the priceGTC 2026: Ian Buck press Q&A transcript — VP of Hyperscale and HPC speaks out on shelving CPX and shipping LPU decode this yearDemand for data center CPUs has surged, and AI agents are responsibleThis massive power consumption is one of the reasons for the opposition against their construction in communities, with residents blaming them for increased utility prices. However, the IEA says that its analysis “does not yet show a clear relationship between growth in data center capacity and increases in electricity prices.” It noted that if a data center uses existing capacity and pays for its share of the cost, then it could potentially lead to lower utility bills for all customers. However, if the grid operator is required to upgrade its system to accommodate the large consumer, then it could also lead to increased monthly bills if the costs are spread across all users.Emissions are another issue that the IEA has raised. Renewable energy dominates data centers’ power purchase agreements at nearly 50%, but actual power generation puts coal- and natural-gas power sources closer to 60%. This is likely due to the need for reliability, with the latter kicking in when the former cannot deliver the power that the data center needs. Aside from that, a few projects are deploying their own power, like Elon Musk’s Colossus 2 in Southaven, Mississippi, with about 180GW planned or under construction in the U.S. So, even though renewable energy is growing to accommodate demand, it’s also expected that coal- and natural-gas emissions from data centers will rise by 70% by 2030.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Investments in AI data centers are expected to hit $32 trillion by 2050, putting the infrastructure spending for the industry larger than railways, electrification, and the internet, combined. Despite that, the IEA says the grid remains a significant bottleneck — renewable power plants take between one and five years to complete, which is around the same time that some massive data center projects take if they do not face an extended moratorium, while transmission works can take three to five times longer. This is probably one of the reasons why some AI hyperscalers are choosing to put jet engines on their sites instead, although these are also facing shortages, especially in turbine blades. items.titleZh: 得益于4万亿美元支出，AI数据中心电力需求到2030年将翻倍，给能源系统增添相当于整个英国的负担
items.descriptionZh:
国际能源署（IEA）《2026年世界能源展望》报告显示，全球AI数据中心的快速扩张正在给各国电网带来巨大压力，许多地区的拟建项目用电需求将超过现有电网峰值负荷能力。目前，全球各类数据中心合计可用容量约为120GW，预计到本十年末还将新增120GW，其中75%将专门用于人工智能。IEA还通过卫星图像跟踪了93个正在建设或扩建的大型“AI工厂”，估算这些站点的容量在短短两年内从不足2GW增长到17GW，全部建成后总容量预计达到50GW，相当于为电力需求再增加一个英国的用电量。

大规模用电也引发了社区反对，居民担心数据中心推高电价。不过，IEA表示，其分析“尚未显示数据中心容量增长与电价上涨之间存在明确关系”。报告指出，如果数据中心利用现有电网容量并承担相应成本，可能反而有助于降低所有用户的电费；但如果电网运营商需要升级系统来容纳这类大型用户，且升级成本分摊给所有用户，月度账单可能上升。

排放问题同样受到关注。数据显示，可再生能源在数据中心电力购买协议中占比接近50%，但实际发电来源中煤炭和天然气接近60%。这很可能是因为数据中心需要稳定可靠的电力供应，当可再生能源无法满足需求时，化石能源会补位。部分项目开始自建电源，例如马斯克位于密西西比州Southaven的Colossus 2；美国还有约180GW的项目处于规划或在建状态。尽管可再生能源装机在增长，IEA仍预计到2030年，数据中心带来的煤炭和天然气排放将增加70%。

投资方面，到2050年，AI数据中心相关投资预计将达到32万亿美元，使该行业的基础设施支出超过铁路、电气化和互联网建设的总和。但IEA认为，电网仍是关键瓶颈：可再生能源电厂建设需要1至5年，大型数据中心项目若不遭遇长期禁令也大约需要类似时间，而输电工程耗时可达前者的3至5倍。这也可能是一些AI超大规模厂商选择在站点部署喷气发动机的原因之一，但这类设备同样面临供应短缺，尤其是涡轮叶片。总体来看，AI数据中心扩张不仅是算力问题，也正在成为电力供应、电网升级、排放和基础设施投资之间的系统性挑战。

items.title: NVIDIA and Microsoft Expand Accelerated Computing From Azure to Windows PCs
items.description: NVIDIA and Microsoft are extending their full-stack collaboration to help organizations build, customize and deploy intelligent applications — from next-generation infrastructure on Azure to industrial systems and Windows PCs. At Microsoft Ignite, the companies are expanding access to Azure virtual machines powered by NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 systems, as well as adding customer availability to […]
items.content: NVIDIA and Microsoft are extending their full-stack collaboration to help organizations build, customize and deploy intelligent applications — from next-generation infrastructure on Azure to industrial systems and Windows PCs. At Microsoft Ignite, the companies are expanding access to Azure virtual machines powered by NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 systems, as well as adding customer availability to NVIDIA open models and customization capabilities through Microsoft Foundry, and new options for running AI at the edge, where businesses generate and use their data. Microsoft is also using NVIDIA technologies to accelerate its own models and services, including NVIDIA Dynamo inference software for post-training and NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs for Bing search models. NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 Running in Azure NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 systems are running in Azure data centers, providing infrastructure designed for demanding reasoning, agentic applications, and large-scale model training and inference. Microsoft and NVIDIA are also collaborating to extend confidential computing to bare-metal and rack-scale AI infrastructure. The work will help protect sensitive models and data while they are being processed, supporting organizations that need to work with proprietary or regulated information. NVIDIA Confidential Computing and attestation help customers verify the computing environment before releasing sensitive models, data or keys. As AI workloads span more interconnected accelerators, the companies are working to extend those protections across the AI factory infrastructure. To help data centers get more performance from available power, NVIDIA and Microsoft are also collaborating on power efficiency using NVIDIA MaxLPS. Azure’s Vera Rubin preview builds on NVIDIA and Microsoft’s codesign and performance optimization, underscored in the latest NVIDIA Blackwell-based MLPerf results. In MLPerf Training v6.1, Azure scaled to 10,240 NVIDIA GPUs with GB200 NVL72 systems on the DeepSeek-V3 model, the largest scale in the round. In MLPerf Inference v6.1, Azure’s NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 systems led cloud submissions on DeepSeek-R1 interactive throughput by over 10%, per Signal65. Helping Enterprises Customize and Deploy Open Models Enterprise AI agents need to reason through complex tasks, find relevant company information and understand business documents. NVIDIA and Microsoft are expanding the models and services available through Microsoft Foundry to help developers bring these capabilities into business applications. Microsoft’s serverless Programmed Training offering gives developers control over post-training workflows while Foundry manages the underlying infrastructure. Enterprises can focus on their business data, evaluating model responses and improving model behavior. Foundry Managed Compute adds support for deploying custom model weights, helping connect model customization with deployment through Microsoft’s managed services. EY used Programmed Training in Microsoft Foundry to adapt NVIDIA Nemotron open models for classifying corporate purchasing records, improving accuracy on its evaluation dataset by 55% and lowering cost by 15x compared with proprietary frontier models. The work demonstrates how enterprises can customize open models for specialized business tasks. The expanded NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 lineup on Foundry Managed Compute supports different requirements across enterprise applications. Nemotron 3.5 Super is designed for long-running agents working across coding, research and business workflows, while Lightning supports applications that need fast responses and tool use. Complementary models help agents find relevant information with Nemotron Embed and Rerank, extract structured information from documents with Nemotron Parse and detect harmful content with Nemotron Content Safety. Nemotron 3.5 Bolt — designed for high-throughput, low-latency reasoning — and Transcribe, for speech recognition, are coming soon. Bringing AI Closer to Enterprise Data NVIDIA and Microsoft are expanding deployment options beyond the cloud, helping organizations run models and agents closer to their data while maintaining control over their infrastructure and operations. Expanded support for Nemotron 3.5 in Foundry Local brings capabilities for reasoning, coding and tool-using agents to Azure Local environments. Retrieval models help applications find evidence across text, document images, charts and tables. Azure Local will also support NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs from hardware partners, giving organizations additional options for deploying AI on premises. Azure Local is expanding to NVIDIA Jetson Thor and Jetson Orin edge AI platforms to support industrial applications such as machine vision, robotics and autonomous operations. NVIDIA physical AI models, including Cosmos, are also being brought to Foundry Local. On Windows PCs powered by NVIDIA RTX Spark, NVIDIA and Microsoft will showcase local large language model experiences at Ignite, demonstrating how developers can run AI applications directly on devices. For organizations using Cloud PCs, the companies are bringing Direct Stream capabilities to GPU-accelerated Windows 365 Cloud PCs. These capabilities support demanding graphics applications with up to two 4K streams at 60 frames per second and low latency, even over challenging networks. A limited preview is open for sign-ups, with public preview planned for early 2027. Connecting Scientific AI With Microsoft Discovery For scientific research, NVIDIA BioNemo Agent Toolkit and NVIDIA ALCHEMI Toolkit are expanding into the Microsoft Discovery catalog, bringing models for life sciences, drug discovery and materials and chemical science into Microsoft’s agentic research platform. BioNeMo Agent Toolkit helps scientists use natural language to run computational biology workflows in Microsoft Discovery, with agents coordinating the tools and model calls needed to carry out the work. An initial integration uses the RFD4-Proteina model, developed in collaboration with the University of Washington’s Institute for Protein Design, to generate candidate protein structures and amino acid sequences for further evaluation and laboratory validation. Accelerating Microsoft’s Models and Services Alongside expanding customer access to NVIDIA technologies, Microsoft is using NVIDIA software and accelerated computing in its own AI development and services. Microsoft AI uses NVIDIA Dynamo to support reinforcement learning rollout inference during post-training. This computationally intensive process generates the experiences used to improve models. Dynamo coordinates inference across a large GPU fleet, optimizing performance, as well as helping manage requests, model updates and recovery from failures. The deployment builds on joint engineering between Microsoft AI and NVIDIA. Visit NVIDIA at Ignite for demonstrations spanning enterprise applications, robotics, accelerated data processing and local computing, with hardware including an NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 rack and RTX Spark devices. View NVIDIA sessions, hands-on labs and booth theater presentations.

items.titleZh: NVIDIA 与微软将加速计算从 Azure 扩展至 Windows PC
items.descriptionZh:
NVIDIA与Microsoft在Microsoft Ignite上宣布扩展全栈合作，目标是帮助企业在从Azure云端到工业系统、边缘设备和Windows PC的完整范围内构建、定制和部署智能应用。背景是企业AI正从试验走向生产，既需要更强的大规模推理、智能体应用和模型训练基础设施，也需要开放模型定制、敏感数据保护、能效优化以及更靠近数据源的边缘部署能力。双方此次合作覆盖AI工厂基础设施、Microsoft Foundry模型定制与部署、边缘AI、科学发现以及微软自身模型和服务加速。

在云端基础设施方面，NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72系统已在Azure数据中心运行，面向高要求的推理、智能体应用以及大规模模型训练和推理。Azure的Vera Rubin预览建立在NVIDIA与Microsoft协同设计和性能优化基础上。双方还将机密计算扩展到裸金属和机架级AI基础设施，帮助保护处理过程中的敏感模型和数据，并通过NVIDIA机密计算与认证机制，在释放敏感模型、数据或密钥前验证计算环境；随着AI工作负载跨越多互联加速器，相关保护也将扩展到AI工厂基础设施。为提升数据中心在可用电力下的性能，双方还基于NVIDIA MaxLPS合作优化能效。性能对比方面，最新Blackwell平台MLPerf结果提供了参考：在MLPerf Training v6.1中，Azure使用GB200 NVL72系统将DeepSeek-V3训练扩展到10,240块NVIDIA GPU，为本轮最大规模；在MLPerf Inference v6.1中，据Signal65，Azure的NVIDIA GB300 NVL72系统在DeepSeek-R1交互吞吐上领先云提交超过10%。

在开放模型与企业定制方面，双方通过Microsoft Foundry扩大模型和服务可用性。Microsoft的无服务器Programmed Training让开发者控制后训练工作流，而Foundry管理底层基础设施，使企业可聚焦业务数据、评估模型响应并改进模型行为；Foundry Managed Compute新增对部署自定义模型权重的支持，把模型定制与通过微软托管服务部署连接起来。EY使用Microsoft Foundry中的Programmed Training适配NVIDIA Nemotron开放模型，对企业采购记录进行分类，在评估数据集上准确率提升55%，成本降至专有前沿模型的1/15（降低15倍），展示了企业针对专门业务任务定制开放模型的可行性。扩展的NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5阵容覆盖不同企业应用需求：Nemotron 3.5 Super面向跨编码、研究和业务工作流的长时运行智能体，Lightning面向需要快速响应和工具使用的应用；Nemotron Embed和Rerank帮助智能体检索相关信息，Nemotron Parse从文档中提取结构化信息，Nemotron Content Safety检测有害内容；面向高吞吐、低延迟推理的Nemotron 3.5 Bolt和语音识别模型Transcribe即将推出。

在边缘和终端方面，双方把部署选项从云扩展到更靠近企业数据的位置，同时保持企业对基础设施和运营的控制。Foundry Local扩展支持Nemotron 3.5，将推理、编码和工具调用智能体能力带到Azure Local环境；检索模型可跨文本、文档图像、图表和表格寻找证据。Azure Local还将支持来自硬件合作伙伴的NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPU，为本地部署AI提供更多选择，并扩展到NVIDIA Jetson Thor和Jetson Orin边缘AI平台，支持机器视觉、机器人、自主运营等工业应用；包括Cosmos在内的NVIDIA物理AI模型也被引入Foundry Local。在搭载NVIDIA RTX Spark的Windows PC上，双方将在Ignite展示本地大语言模型体验，说明开发者可直接在设备上运行AI应用。对于使用云PC的组织，双方将Direct Stream能力引入GPU加速的Windows 365 Cloud PC，支持高要求图形应用以低延迟实现最多两路4K 60帧/秒流，即使网络条件具有挑战性；该能力已开放有限预览注册，计划于2027年初进入公共预览。

在科学AI方面，NVIDIA BioNeMo Agent Toolkit和NVIDIA ALCHEMI Toolkit正在进入Microsoft Discovery目录，把生命科学、药物发现以及材料与化学科学模型引入微软的智能体研究平台。BioNeMo Agent Toolkit帮助科学家用自然语言在Microsoft Discovery中运行计算生物学工作流，由智能体协调所需工具和模型调用；初始集成采用与华盛顿大学蛋白质设计研究所合作开发的RFD4-Proteina模型，生成候选蛋白质结构和氨基酸序列，供进一步评估和实验室验证。与此同时，Microsoft也在用NVIDIA技术加速自身模型和服务：Microsoft AI使用NVIDIA Dynamo支持后训练中的强化学习rollout推理，Dynamo在大规模GPU集群上协调推理、优化性能，并帮助管理请求、模型更新和故障恢复；Bing搜索模型则使用NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPU加速。整体来看，这一合作把云端AI工厂、开放模型定制、边缘与PC部署、科学发现和微软自身服务连接为全栈体系，使企业能够在Azure、本地和边缘环境中部署智能体应用，并在性能、成本、数据主权与合规之间取得平衡。

items.title: Into the Omniverse: How Developers Turn Ideas Into Simulations With Frontier AI Agents
items.description: Turning a simulation idea into a working application means assembling assets, connecting physics and rendering, and checking that the scene behaves as intended. items.content: Turning a simulation idea into a working application means assembling assets, connecting physics and rendering, and checking that the scene behaves as intended. Developers are combining frontier AI models with NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to help carry out that work — building applications for exploring scenarios, investigating failures and improving designs. Developers direct AI agents through natural-language instructions, review results and guide changes. Omniverse libraries provide GPU-accelerated physics, rendering and sensor simulation capabilities. Explore the projects below to see frontier AI models such as GPT-6 Astra at work, and check back for new examples from NVIDIA teams and developers across the ecosystem. Physical AI Paves the Path to Autonomous Industrial Operations 🔗 https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Nyhamna_footage_take5_30s.mp4 AI agents powered by frontier models pave the way to autonomous operations. They use industrial tools and engineering data to help engineers build digital twins that test plans and processes and evaluate operational decisions. Falkor, a KONGSBERG company, shows how this works in practice. The company’s Falkor Surface platform lets customers turn their computer-aided design and engineering data into facility-scale digital twins using the GPT-6 Astra model. The platform uses NVIDIA Omniverse libraries and NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Server Edition GPUs on Microsoft Azure to enable advanced physics simulation. AI agents built on Falkor’s agentic engine understand dense technical documentation, spatial relationships and real-world physics. Engineers can create and test plans in simulation before traveling on site, reducing costly delays and mistakes. They can also inspect equipment and check clearances in a shared view. Read Falkor’s article and watch the livestream for a closer look at how the company builds these tools and checks the agents’ work. Build a Robot Pick-and-Place Simulation With SimReady Assets 🔗 Getting a robot model into a scene is only the start. Developers also need to assemble its components, add controls and check whether it can complete a task. NVIDIA developers Dillon Bailey and Rishabh Chadha used 3D assets from the SimReady Central library to build a pick-and-place simulation of a robot moving a can using the NVIDIA Isaac Sim framework. They directed an agent equipped with GPT-6 Sol and Isaac Sim skills to assemble the scene and generate pick-and-place controls. Testing the assembled scene shows how the assets work together, from joint movement and contact behavior to the gripper’s ability to hold, move and release the can. With that baseline in place, developers can adjust object positions and motion paths and repeat the tests to evaluate how each change affects the task. Follow the walkthrough to assemble and test a pick-and-place simulation in Isaac Sim, with sample agent prompts and checks for robot movement and grasp behavior. Build a Voice-Controlled VR Simulation With SimReady Assets 🔗 Bringing 3D assets into virtual reality (VR) requires more than rendering a scene. Objects need to respond to controllers and behave as expected when grabbed, moved or released. NVIDIA Omniverse community developer Michael Wagner took on this challenge. He directed GPT-6 Astra to use Blender software to model a study environment from two reference images, balancing visual quality with efficient performance in VR. He then used Claude Code to build an application that lets users find SimReady Central assets by voice and interact with them in an immersive VR scene. The Claude Code agent worked for about eight hours, and Wagner built the application over a weekend using an NVIDIA RTX 6000 Ada workstation and a Meta Quest 3 VR headset. The application ran on NVIDIA Omniverse libraries: ovstage shared the OpenUSD scene, ovrtx rendered it, ovxr enabled VR and ovphysx ran physics. Wagner later built a second version with ovnewton, which integrates with ovstage, to compare the physics libraries. The biggest challenge for Wagner was checking what happened inside the headset. Automated tests missed problems he could feel, including objects shaking when grabbed. Wagner reported the symptoms, guided the agent through changes and verified the interaction himself. Updating the grab control once per frame resolved the shaking. His takeaway: Give agents renders and logs to inspect, then check the experience directly. Explore his open source demo for build instructions, a starting prompt and reusable agent skills. Send Microducks on Rounds in a Simulated Hospital 🔗 https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/microducks-icu-pathtraced-16x9-1920x1080-1.mp4 Before adapting a robot to a new environment, developers need to test whether its walking policy — the AI that controls how it moves — can keep it stable in that setting. AI developer Maziyar Panahi directed Claude Code, using Claude Opus 5.5, to assemble an intensive care unit from 13 NVIDIA SimReady hospital assets and test Microduck robots inside it. The assets came with Newton physics settings, so Panahi didn’t have to model the furniture or create collision geometry from scratch. The Newton physics engine also helped replicate the ward so hundreds of copies could run together on one NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 GPU. When the cloud containers lacked graphics support, Panahi and the Claude Code agent separated simulation from rendering, recording robot poses in the cloud and rendering them locally. They also treated the furniture as static collision objects, which enabled larger runs within the solver’s limits. The robots walked using AI they had already been trained on and followed preset points along a route. Panahi checked how many robots remained upright: In a 256-ward run, 766 of 768 Microducks were still standing after 14 simulated seconds. He said the agent’s work took about two hours. Explore the open source demo for a starter prompt, checks and instructions to begin with one ward on a CPU, then scale to hundreds on an NVIDIA GPU. Create Editable 3D Assets With Houdini and AI Agents 🔗 Creating animated 3D content requires connecting modeling, simulation, materials and rendering. Nick Scarcella, a senior technical artist on NVIDIA’s BondLab team, directed AI agents — primarily using Claude — to work with CUDA libraries and Isaac Sim to create animations. The BondLab team uses SideFX Houdini and the NVIDIA ovrtx library to develop materials, lighting and the final rendered appearance. In one experiment, Scarcella guided Astra to recreate an OP-1 portable synthesizer using product images, manuals and technical direction. He exported the model into the OpenUSD framework, tested it in Houdini and Blender, then used Astra and Opus to refine details before adjusting materials and textures for ovrtx rendering. Scarcella also used a publicly shared robot-hand checkpoint in Isaac Sim, directing the motion and developing materials and lighting in Houdini with Claude’s assistance. Working with team member Steven Dvornik, the team created an “Echos” visualization: translucent versions of the hand overlap and merge into a single hand animation, offering a visual interpretation of robot training. https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Robot_Hand_Video_Omniverse.mp4 Figure: An artistic visualization of simulated robot-hand motion, developed with AI assistance and Houdini’s materials and lighting tools. These workflows bring agent-assisted creation into existing artist tools, giving teams editable content they can inspect, refine and render across applications. Explore Scarcella’s Houdini MCP tools and agent skill. Test Robotic Disassembly With Computer-Aided Design and Simulation 🔗 Before a robot can disassemble a product, developers need to know whether its tools can reach and remove the parts. Jens Jebens, a senior product manager for OpenUSD at NVIDIA, directed Astra to model a car suspension in PTC Onshape and configure it in NVIDIA Isaac Sim. Jebens used simulation feedback to revise the tooling, including a wrench designed to reach the suspension’s bolts, and reported successful removal of a suspension component in simulation. https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Robotic_Dissasembly_Omniverse.mp4 PTC also connects computer-aided design (CAD) with simulation through Onshape’s SimReady Publisher, built with NVIDIA Omniverse libraries. Robotics startup Sensori uses it to transfer its Yuri robot into Isaac Sim, carrying geometry, joints and configuration data so the team can evaluate design changes without repeatedly rebuilding the simulation model. Read Sensori’s story. Explore the Onshape importer guide. Create an Editable Building Model From Site Scans 🔗 https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/relay-video-v14-1080p.mp4 Planning warehouse automation requires a model of the building itself, but shelving and machinery can obscure its structure in site scans. Omniverse brings together real-to-sim tools and agent skills to help developers turn real-world captures into editable starting environments for physical AI simulation. David Wehr, from NVIDIA’s simulation technology team, built on that work using Astra to develop a workflow for digitally reconstructing a building without its contents. The goal is an editable, simulation-ready building model where developers can add or reposition shelving and machinery to evaluate warehouse layouts and automation plans before making physical changes. Wehr guided Astra to interpret panoramic photos, create building geometry and align it with point-cloud measurements. OpenUSD stores the models, while Omniverse’s ovrtx library renders results for inspection. Explore NVIDIA Omniverse agent skills to help agents build with Omniverse libraries. Test Gas-Turbine Operating Scenarios With a Digital Twin 🔗 https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Turbine-Lab-RTX-and-What-If-under-10MB-1.mp4 Before changing how industrial equipment operates, engineers need a way to explore the consequences. Pradeep Kaushik, a member of the NVIDIA Omniverse developer relations team, directed Astra to build a what-if analysis application around a simulated gas turbine and generator. The application lets users adjust conditions such as load, ambient temperature and fuel composition, then compare power, efficiency, fuel consumption and equipment response. Six test procedures explore scenarios including load changes, a stuck fuel valve and an exhaust-sensor error. The prototype gives engineers an interactive way to investigate how operating changes and faults could affect equipment behavior, supporting decisions about which scenarios warrant further testing. Astra used tools like Cantera for thermochemistry and SciPy for equipment dynamics. The application maps solver results to rotor animation and color-coded temperature, pressure and flow-velocity indicators in a 3D turbine. NVIDIA Omniverse libraries update the scene (ovstage), render it with RTX (ovrtx) and stream the view to the browser (ovstream). Engineers can rotate and zoom the cutaway, switch between indicators, and pause or scrub through a simulated response alongside charts and virtual instruments. Build Simulation Scenes With Open Source SimReady Assets 🔗 https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/kitchen_final_blog_with_music.mp4 With SimReady Central Library, announced at GTC Berlin, developers can access more than 2,000 simulation-ready USD assets from equipment manufacturers and asset providers for robotics simulations and AI factory digital twins workflows. Paul Kind, a member of NVIDIA’s Omniverse documentation team, pointed an AI agent to the library and guided scene assembly through conversation. His kitchen scene included 180 placements drawn from 63 unique library assets, alongside 18 custom geometry pieces. Kind reviewed renders produced with Isaac Sim and guided further adjustments. For robotics and factory workflows, developers can select SimReady assets with the simulation properties embedded to fit their required task then test in an assembled environment. Find assets in SimReady Central Library, and learn how to contribute. Stress-Test a Warehouse Simulation at Scale 🔗 https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Infra-scale-demo-20260914_144614-Meeting-Recording.mp4 A warehouse simulation needs to keep running smoothly as more robot arms, conveyors and boxes fill the scene. When it slows down, developers need to identify what’s holding it back. Bhavik Sanganee, principal engineer at NVIDIA, used Astra with NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to build a warehouse simulation, increase its complexity and investigate slowdowns. Performance first fell below the target when the scene doubled in size. Running physics calculations, image rendering and video preparation concurrently restored performance and enabled further scaling. With 80 conveyors, 40 arms and 800 boxes, the simulation sustained 30 frames per second at full HD resolution during a two-minute test. The arms completed 640 successful box placements. Doubling the scene again reduced performance. Testing traced the slowdown to the physics and robot-control pipeline, giving Sanganee a specific area to improve. Start building with NVIDIA Omniverse libraries. Test Robot Control for Flexible Cable Routing 🔗 https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/scurve_rl_vs_astra_side_by_side.mp4 In electronics assembly, a robot may need to position a flexible cable around components before plugging it into a port. The cable bends as the robot moves it, and the connector must line up precisely to fit. Oyindamola Omotuyi, robotics technical marketing manager at NVIDIA, directed Astra to build a robot simulation using NVIDIA Isaac Lab, Newton physics and Omniverse rendering with a Robotiq gripper handling the cable. Astra also developed a reinforcement learning system that combined learned cable-routing movements with position-and-orientation feedback and corrective adjustments for USB-C insertion. The simulation gave Omotuyi a way to test cable handling and connector alignment before moving to physical-robot experiments. The controller used information supplied directly by the simulation. Next steps include testing a friction-held grasp and using information a physical robot could obtain from cameras and sensors. Get started with robot learning in NVIDIA Isaac Lab. Turn Robot Computer-Aided Design Into a SimReady Asset 🔗 Before testing whether a robot can pick up and move a box, developers need a simulation model with joints that move correctly and with grippers that can hold the object. A computer-aided design (CAD) model provides the robot’s shape, but it still needs physics properties to perform the task. Using an ABB Robotics YuMi robot, developers directed Astra with NVIDIA Omniverse content libraries to convert CAD files into OpenUSD, match the robot’s appearance to reference images, and configure joints and collision geometry. They checked the asset against SimReady Foundation requirements before testing it in NVIDIA Isaac Sim. Both arms and grippers completed four cube pick-and-place cycles, using simulated finger contact and friction. These tests demonstrated behavior under the simulated conditions — estimated physical properties were not calibrated against the real robot. Follow the five-step SimReady tutorial. Build a Humanoid Simulator for a Warehouse Environment 🔗 https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Humanoid-Warehouse.mp4 Explore a gamified, physics-based control of a humanoid robot in first- and third-person view. Before automating warehouse tasks, developers need an interactive simulation environment to explore task behavior and evaluate how the work gets done. Frank DeLise, Omniverse product manager at NVIDIA, used Astra to turn a SimReady warehouse and humanoid robot into an interactive simulator with first- and third-person views. DeLise directed Astra to connect NVIDIA Omniverse libraries for physics (ovphysx), scene updates (ovstage), rendering (ovrtx) and the user interface (ovui). He also used Astra with SimReady (simready-foundation) to create the physical scene in simulation. Astra then generated animation and application code to bring those capabilities together. Learn how to prepare and validate SimReady robot assets with frontier AI models and NVIDIA Omniverse libraries. Connect an Autonomous-Driving Testing Workflow 🔗 https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/zero-to-alpamayo-under-10MB.mp4 Changing a scene, sensor or driving model can significantly affect autonomous-vehicle simulations. Doyub Kim, a manager on the simulation technology team at NVIDIA, asked Astra to build Zero to Alpamayo — a reusable simulation environment based on San Francisco’s Market Street. Kim directed Astra to map out the workflow, then connect asset creation, traffic, Omniverse RTX sensor simulation and Alpamayo driving in stages, checking each integration. The resulting prototype was a testing ground for comparing models and tracing how scene or sensor changes affect downstream driving behavior. A separate Cosmos3-Nano experiment varied weather and lighting in recorded simulation videos, allowing Kim to compare the driving model’s responses to the same scenario under different conditions. Use Sensor Differences to Create and Improve Digital Twins 🔗 https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/0_00-0_004-hubble_rivermark_Real_Sim_no_loop.mp4 Comparing recorded and simulated camera and lidar outputs gives developers key performance indicator-based feedback for refining a scene. To test robots and autonomous vehicles, developers need to know how closely simulated sensors match real ones. Ashley Reid, who works on RTX sensor validation at NVIDIA, directed Astra and Claude Fable 5 agents to compare ovrtx camera and raw LiDAR outputs with recorded data. The agents created two digital twins from scratch and improved two existing ones. Over about three days, Reid guided an iterative workflow in which agents measured differences, created or modified OpenUSD scenes, and checked the results. Changes addressed missing objects, geometry and materials, with acceptance depending on camera and LiDAR metrics. This gives developers a way to use measured discrepancies to guide scene creation and improvement. Start by rendering an OpenUSD scene with the ovrtx minimal Python example, then define a sensor measure to compare with recorded data. Robo Olympics: Test Robot Skills With Simulation 🔗 Teaching robots new movements means checking whether those actions work under physical constraints. Tae Kim, who leads NVIDIA Omniverse engineering and product, used sports videos and natural-language instructions to guide Astra in building Robo Olympics, an experimental project that tests simulated Unitree G1 humanoids performing sports movements. Under Kim’s direction, Astra built controllers and refined them through physics trials. Newton Physics Engine simulated behavior, the open source NVIDIA Warp framework accelerated calculations and ovrtx rendered scenes and virtual-camera images. In one experiment, the robot cleared a single hurdle in 64 of 100 simulation trials. The trials gave Kim feedback for improving the robot’s timing and control. Watch Kim explore building simulations with Astra and NVIDIA Omniverse libraries. Bring the International Space Station Into the Browser 🔗 Turning 3D models into an application requires connecting assets, live data and an interface. Nic Johns, an engineering director at NVIDIA, prompted Astra to assemble NASA assets into an OpenUSD International Space Station model with telemetry. Johns built the application with a single prompt, then used a follow-up prompt to shift the scene to Earth’s daytime side so the planet was visible. The workflow used Blender for asset preparation and Omniverse libraries for rendering (ovrtx), scene runtime (ovstage) and streaming (ovstream). The application brings 3D models and operational data into the browser, with Johns guiding its development through prompts and corrections. Try the Omniverse Real-Time Viewer skill. Turn Captured Rooms Into Testing Environments 🔗 A digitally reconstructed room needs editable objects and accurate physical behavior before developers can test interactions. Chirag Majithia, from the Isaac engineering applications team at NVIDIA, directed Astra to turn stereo camera captures into an editable OpenUSD studio. The workflow combined PyCuSFM, FoundationStereo and nvblox for reconstruction, with user review guiding object selection and placement. Astra assembled generated and Blender-authored assets and used USD Content Agents to configure how objects move and interact in simulation. Isaac Sim tests guided collision and contact revisions for doors and drawers. The studio connects captured geometry to interaction testing, making gaps and object behavior easier to inspect. Explore USD Content Agents. Have a simulation idea? Explore NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to start building with an AI agent.

items.titleZh: 走进 Omniverse：开发者如何借助前沿 AI 智能体将创意转化为仿真
items.descriptionZh:
NVIDIA发布的技术博客展示了其推动仿真应用开发的新范式：开发者不再从零编写所有场景、物理和渲染代码，而是通过自然语言指挥前沿AI模型，如GPT-6 Astra、GPT-6 Sol、Claude Opus 5.5、Claude Fable 5等，结合NVIDIA Omniverse库完成资产组装、物理与渲染连接、场景验证和迭代优化。Omniverse库提供GPU加速的物理、渲染和传感器仿真能力，OpenUSD作为统一场景描述格式，SimReady资产则内嵌物理属性，使AI代理能够理解空间关系、技术文档和现实物理，帮助工程师和艺术家快速构建可用于机器人、自动驾驶、工业数字孪生和VR等场景的仿真环境。博客中的多个案例说明，这种“AI代理+Omniverse+SimReady资产”的工作流正在覆盖从工业运营到内容创作、从机器人技能测试到自动驾驶验证的广泛领域。

在工业自主运营方面，KONGSBERG旗下Falkor的Falkor Surface平台使用GPT-6 Astra，将计算机辅助设计和工程数据转化为设施级数字孪生，底层采用NVIDIA Omniverse库和运行于Microsoft Azure的NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Server Edition GPU。基于Falkor代理引擎构建的AI代理能够理解密集技术文档、空间关系和现实物理，工程师可在仿真中创建并测试计划、检查设备和间隙，再前往现场，从而减少昂贵延误和错误。机器人拾放案例中，NVIDIA开发者Dillon Bailey和Rishabh Chadha使用SimReady Central库的3D资产，在Isaac Sim中构建机器人移动罐体的拾放仿真，并由配备GPT-6 Sol和Isaac Sim技能的代理组装场景、生成拾放控制。测试覆盖关节运动、接触行为以及夹爪抓取、移动和释放罐体的能力；建立基线后，开发者可调整物体位置和运动路径并重复测试，评估每次改动对任务的影响。

VR方面，Omniverse社区开发者Michael Wagner用GPT-6 Astra指导Blender根据两张参考图建模学习环境，在视觉质量与VR性能之间平衡，再用Claude Code构建可通过语音查找SimReady Central资产并在沉浸式VR中交互的应用。Claude Code代理工作约8小时，Wagner用一个周末在NVIDIA RTX 6000 Ada工作站和Meta Quest 3头显上完成应用。该应用运行于Omniverse库：ovstage共享OpenUSD场景，ovrtx渲染，ovxr支持VR，ovphysx运行物理；第二版使用ovnewton并与ovstage集成以比较物理库。最大挑战是检查头显内部体验，自动测试漏掉了抓取时物体抖动等他可感知的问题；通过报告症状、引导代理修改并亲自验证，最终将抓取控制改为每帧更新一次解决了抖动。他的经验是给代理提供渲染和日志供检查，同时必须直接体验。

医疗物流案例中，AI开发者Maziyar Panahi指导Claude Code使用Claude Opus 5.5，从13个NVIDIA SimReady医院资产组装ICU并测试Microduck机器人。资产自带Newton物理设置，无需从头建模家具或创建碰撞几何；Newton物理引擎还帮助复制病房，使数百个副本可在一个NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 GPU上运行。云容器缺乏图形支持时，Panahi和代理将仿真与渲染分离，在云端记录机器人位姿、本地渲染；同时将家具视为静态碰撞对象，以在求解器限制内扩大运行规模。机器人使用已训练AI和预设路径行走。在256个病房的运行中，768个Microducks在14个仿真秒后仍有766个站立；代理工作约2小时。该开源演示提供起始提示、检查项和从单个CPU病房扩展到GPU数百病房的说明。

内容创作方面，NVIDIA BondLab团队高级技术美术Nick Scarcella主要使用Claude指导AI代理，结合CUDA库和Isaac Sim创建动画。团队使用SideFX Houdini和NVIDIA ovrtx库开发材质、灯光和最终渲染外观。实验中，Scarcella引导Astra根据产品图片、手册和技术指导重建OP-1便携合成器，导出到OpenUSD，在Houdini和Blender中测试，再用Astra和Opus细化细节，调整材质纹理以供ovrtx渲染。他还使用Isaac Sim中公开共享的机器人手检查点，在Claude协助下指导动作并在Houdini中开发材质和灯光；与团队成员Steven Dvornik创建“Echos”可视化：半透明手部版本重叠并合并为单一手部动画，作为机器人训练的视觉诠释。这些工作流将代理辅助创作带入现有艺术家工具，生成可检查、细化和跨应用渲染的可编辑内容，并开源了Houdini MCP工具和代理技能。

机器人拆解测试中，NVIDIA OpenUSD高级产品经理Jens Jebens指导Astra在PTC Onshape中建模汽车悬架并在Isaac Sim中配置，利用仿真反馈修改工具，包括设计用于触及悬架螺栓的扳手，并报告在仿真中成功拆下悬架部件。PTC还通过基于Omniverse库构建的Onshape SimReady Publisher连接CAD与仿真；机器人初创公司Sensori用它将其Yuri机器人转入Isaac Sim，携带几何、关节和配置数据，使团队无需反复重建仿真模型即可评估设计变更。建筑重建案例中，NVIDIA仿真技术团队的David Wehr使用Astra开发工作流，在不含内部物品的情况下数字化重建建筑。目标是得到可编辑、仿真就绪的建筑模型，开发者可添加或重新定位货架和机械，在物理改造前评估仓库布局和自动化计划。Astra被引导解释全景照片、创建建筑几何并与点云测量对齐；OpenUSD存储模型，ovrtx渲染结果供检查。

燃气轮机数字孪生案例中，NVIDIA Omniverse开发者关系团队成员Pradeep Kaushik指导Astra围绕模拟燃气轮机和发电机构建what-if分析应用。用户可调整负荷、环境温度和燃料成分等条件，比较功率、效率、燃料消耗和设备响应；六个测试程序覆盖负荷变化、燃料阀卡滞和排气传感器错误等场景。该原型为工程师提供交互方式，用于调查运行变化和故障如何影响设备行为，支持判断哪些场景值得进一步测试。Astra使用Cantera进行热化学计算、SciPy进行设备动力学计算；应用将求解结果映射到转子动画和颜色编码的温度、压力、流速指示器，Omniverse库分别用ovstage更新场景、ovrtx渲染、ovstream将视图流式传输到浏览器，用户可旋转缩放剖面、切换指标、暂停或拖动模拟响应，并查看图表和虚拟仪器。

SimReady Central Library在GTC Berlin发布，提供来自设备制造商和资产提供商的2000多个仿真就绪USD资产，面向机器人仿真和AI工厂数字孪生工作流。NVIDIA Omniverse文档团队成员Paul Kind将AI代理指向该库，通过对话指导场景组装；其厨房场景包含来自63个独特库资产的180个放置，以及18个自定义几何部件，并用Isaac Sim审查渲染、指导进一步调整。仓库规模压力测试中，NVIDIA首席工程师Bhavik Sanganee使用Astra和Omniverse库构建仓库仿真、增加复杂度并调查变慢原因。场景规模翻倍时性能首次低于目标；并发运行物理计算、图像渲染和视频准备后恢复性能并支持进一步扩展。在80个传送带、40个机械臂和800个箱子的场景中，两分钟测试期间仿真在全高清分辨率下保持30帧/秒，机械臂完成640次成功箱子放置。场景再翻倍后性能下降，测试将瓶颈定位到物理和机器人控制流水线，为改进提供了具体方向。

柔性电缆布线案例中，NVIDIA机器人技术营销经理Oyindamola Omotuyi指导Astra使用NVIDIA Isaac Lab、Newton物理和Omniverse渲染构建机器人仿真，由Robotiq夹爪处理电缆。Astra还开发了强化学习系统，将学习到的电缆布线运动与位置姿态反馈以及USB-C插入的纠正调整相结合。仿真让Omotuyi在进入物理机器人实验前测试电缆处理和连接器对准，控制器直接使用仿真提供的信息；下一步包括测试摩擦保持抓取，并使用物理机器人可通过相机和传感器获取的信息。机器人CAD转SimReady资产案例使用ABB Robotics YuMi机器人，开发者指导Astra和Omniverse内容库将CAD文件转为OpenUSD、匹配机器人外观与参考图，并配置关节和碰撞几何；在Isaac Sim测试前按SimReady Foundation要求检查资产。双臂和夹爪完成四轮立方体拾放，使用模拟手指接触和摩擦。测试展示了模拟条件下的行为，但估计的物理属性未针对真实机器人校准，博客提供五步SimReady教程。

仓库人形机器人模拟器案例中，NVIDIA Omniverse产品经理Frank DeLise使用Astra将SimReady仓库和人形机器人变成具有第一和第三人称视角的交互式模拟器，指导Astra连接Omniverse库的物理ovphysx、场景更新ovstage、渲染ovrtx和用户界面ovui，并用Astra与SimReady（simready-foundation）创建物理场景，随后生成动画和应用代码整合能力。自动驾驶测试工作流案例中，NVIDIA仿真技术团队经理Doyub Kim要求Astra构建“Zero to Alpamayo”——基于旧金山Market街的可复用仿真环境。Astra被指导规划工作流，分阶段连接资产创建、交通、Omniverse RTX传感器仿真和Alpamayo驾驶，并检查每个集成。原型成为比较模型、追踪场景或传感器变化如何影响下游驾驶行为的测试场；另一项Cosmos3-Nano实验改变录制仿真视频中的天气和光照，以比较驾驶模型对同一场景在不同条件下的响应。传感器差异案例中，NVIDIA RTX传感器验证团队的Ashley Reid指导Astra和Claude Fable 5代理比较ovrtx相机和原始LiDAR输出与记录数据。代理从头创建两个数字孪生并改进两个现有数字孪生；约三天内，Reid引导迭代工作流，让代理测量差异、创建或修改OpenUSD场景并检查结果。更改解决缺失对象、几何和材质问题，接受与否取决于相机和LiDAR指标，从而利用测量差异指导场景创建和改进。

Robo Olympics实验中，负责NVIDIA Omniverse工程和产品的Tae Kim使用体育视频和自然语言指令指导Astra构建实验项目，测试模拟Unitree G1人形机器人执行体育动作。Astra构建控制器并通过物理试验改进；Newton物理引擎模拟行为，开源NVIDIA Warp框架加速计算，ovrtx渲染场景和虚拟相机图像。一项实验中，机器人100次仿真试验中有64次越过单个栏架，试验为改进机器人时机和控制提供了反馈。国际空间站案例中，NVIDIA工程总监Nic Johns提示Astra将NASA资产组装成带遥测的OpenUSD国际空间站模型；他用单条提示构建应用，再用后续提示将场景移到地球白天侧以显示行星。工作流使用Blender准备资产，Omniverse库负责渲染ovrtx、场景运行时ovstage和流式传输ovstream，将3D模型和运行数据带入浏览器。房间捕获转测试环境案例中，NVIDIA Isaac工程应用团队的Chirag Majithia指导Astra将立体相机捕获转为可编辑OpenUSD工作室。工作流结合PyCuSFM、FoundationStereo和nvblox进行重建，由用户审查指导对象选择和放置；Astra组装生成资产和Blender创作资产，并使用USD Content Agents配置对象在仿真中的移动和交互。Isaac Sim测试指导门和抽屉的碰撞与接触修订，使捕获几何与交互测试连接，更易检查间隙和对象行为。

总体来看，这些案例的核心创新在于把前沿AI模型从“生成代码”推进到“参与仿真工程全流程”：自然语言指令被转化为场景组装、资产转换、物理配置、控制生成、强化学习、测试检查和结果分析；Omniverse以OpenUSD和GPU加速库统一物理、渲染、传感器仿真与流式部署；SimReady资产和开源代理技能降低复用门槛。性能数据表明，经过并发流水线、仿真与渲染分离、静态碰撞简化等优化，复杂场景可达到数百机器人副本、80传送带/40机械臂/800箱子下全高清30帧/秒、两分钟640次放置等规模；同时机器人站立率766/768、跨栏成功率64/100等指标为迭代提供量化反馈。其技术影响是显著降低数字孪生、机器人测试、自动驾驶验证、VR内容、建筑与工业规划的门槛，使工程师和艺术家能更快探索方案、调查故障并改进设计；但案例也强调人类仍需审查渲染和日志、直接体验VR交互，并对仿真物理属性与真实设备进行校准。应用场景已覆盖工业自主运营、机器人拾放与拆解、医疗物流、VR创作、燃气轮机运行分析、仓库自动化、柔性电缆布线、人形机器人、自动驾驶、传感器数字孪生、机器人运动技能、空间站可视化和真实房间重建测试等。

items.title: Supermicro sued by shareholders over claims Nvidia executive’s wife knew about illicit China sales
items.description: A civil lawsuit claimed that there was "no way Cenly Chen lacked knowledge about the company's illicit sales."
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Instagram Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter More information about the alleged knowledge of chip diversion by a Supermicro executive is being revealed as shareholders’ civil lawsuit against the company progresses. According to The Telegraph, the investors alleged that there was “no way Cenly Chen lacked knowledge about the company’s illicit sales.” Chen, the former Chief Growth Officer at Supermicro and described by a colleague as the company’s sales leader, resigned from her position in April of this year — about a month after the three Supermicro employees, including its co-founder Yih-Shyan “Wally” Liaw, were arrested for a $2.5-billion AI GPU smuggling scheme.Cenly Chen is married to former Nvidia Executive Vice President of Worldwide Field Operations Jay Puri, who is also described as the company’s sales chief. The Information also called him Jensen Huang’s right-hand man and said he was the person that Nvidia’s customers turned to if they wanted to buy chips or had other pressing concerns. The shareholders’ accusations and her relationship with Puri have put the former Supermicro executive in the spotlight, especially after Huang’s sudden departure from the AI chipmaker amid a flurry of affairs and smuggling accusations.Sources say that Puri controlled the AI chip allocations to server manufacturers, including Supermicro, while the lawsuit claims that Chen decided how many Nvidia racks each Supermicro customer could get. A former Supermicro employee was also quoted in the complaint saying that it was “widely known within the Company that Chen had to leave because she had sent emails requesting that Nvidia release chips with serial numbers associated with the GPUs illegally diverted to customers in China.” This apparently refers to the serial numbers that were moved from real to dummy servers using a hairdryer.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Supermicro has said multiple times that it has cooperated with the U.S. government regarding the smuggling investigation and that it has not been included in the lawsuit against the three defendants. Furthermore, the company has denied her involvement regarding Nvidia GPU allocations. “Chen did not manage Supermicro’s relationship with Nvidia and did not decide how Nvidia GPUs were distributed to customers,” a Supermicro spokesperson told The Information. They also said that she left voluntarily and that her LinkedIn profile now reads her current position as CEO of ChronoScale, an Nvidia cloud partner based in Silicon Valley. As for Puri, he stepped away from his position at Nvidia in late August, about two months before the Jensen Huang scandal blew up, although he remains as an advisor to the AI chipmaker. items.titleZh: Supermicro sued by shareholders over claims Nvidia executive’s wife knew about illicit China sales
items.descriptionZh:
美国AI服务器厂商Supermicro（超微电脑）股东民事诉讼披露的新细节，将该公司前首席增长官Cenly Chen推到聚光灯下。案件背景是：三名Supermicro员工——包括联合创始人Yih-Shyan“Wally”Liaw——因涉嫌参与规模达25亿美元的Nvidia AI GPU走私计划被捕；约一个月后，Cenly Chen于今年4月辞去Supermicro职务。股东原告称，作为公司销售负责人之一，Chen“不可能不知道公司的非法销售”。诉状还称，Chen的丈夫Jay Puri是Nvidia前全球现场运营执行副总裁、被外界视为黄仁勋的“左右手”，在Nvidia客户购买芯片等事务中具有重要影响力；据称Puri掌控对包括Supermicro在内的服务器厂商的AI芯片分配，而Chen则决定Supermicro各客户能获得多少Nvidia机架。Supermicro对此否认，称Chen没有管理公司与Nvidia的关系，也没有决定Nvidia GPU如何分配给客户，并强调她系自愿离职；公司还表示已就走私调查配合美国政府，且未被列入针对三名被告的诉讼。Chen目前担任Nvidia云合作伙伴ChronoScale的CEO。Puri已于8月下旬离开Nvidia职位，但仍担任顾问。

从技术规避手法看，本案的关键并非芯片架构创新，而是利用AI GPU供应链追踪与出口管制审计的漏洞。高端Nvidia GPU受美国对华出口限制，序列号是识别GPU身份、核验库存和追踪最终用户的重要标识。诉状引述前Supermicro员工称，公司内部“广泛知道”Chen必须离开，因为她曾发邮件要求Nvidia放行与非法转售至中国客户GPU相关的序列号；这些序列号据称被从真实服务器转移到“假服务器/空壳服务器”上，过程中使用了吹风机。其效果是让受控GPU在账面上看似仍留在合规客户或真实设备中，从而掩盖芯片实际流向中国客户。这种手法说明，出口管制不仅依赖芯片性能限制，也高度依赖序列号、资产标签和服务器整机核验；一旦分配权、销售关系和序列号管理交织，审计链条就可能被利用。

从数据和时间线看，刑事案件涉及约25亿美元AI GPU走私规模，三名Supermicro员工被捕；Chen在逮捕约一个月后辞职，Puri在8月下旬离任Nvidia，报道称这约在相关丑闻发酵前两个月。股东民事诉讼与刑事案件相互独立，但原告试图用Chen与Puri的夫妻关系及其销售职责，证明她对非法销售并非不知情。Supermicro则把责任边界划在公司与Nvidia关系及GPU分配之外。该案的影响不限于一家服务器厂商：它暴露了AI GPU从Nvidia到OEM/ODM、再到云服务商和中国客户的分配与合规风险，可能推动服务器厂商加强序列号核验、最终用户审查和高管利益冲突披露；对Nvidia而言，渠道分配权和销售高层关系也将面临更严格审视。应用场景集中在AI数据中心GPU采购、云GPU服务和受出口管制的服务器整机流通，核心问题是高价值、稀缺AI芯片在分配、转售和跨境交付中的可追踪性。

items.title: Three 'e-waste' Nvidia V100s hit 100 tokens per second on Qwen 3.6 35B in a $1,042 homelab rig
items.description: A homelab builder runs Qwen 3.6 35B on three used Nvidia Tesla V100 GPUs at about 100 tokens per second, in a $1,042 build.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Instagram Share this article 7 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter A homelab builder benchmarked three used Nvidia V100s on Qwen 3.6 35B, achieving about 100 tokens per second in a custom setup costing $1,042 with just “e-waste” GPUs. The smaller, dense Qwen 3.6 27B manages about 24 tokens per second on the same platform, and the V100s use about half the energy of the same number of P100s for a given job.A ~$1k GPU box full of "e-waste" (V100, P100) cards competes with modern hardware/inference APIs. Benchmarking Results incl. power consumption: from r/homelabThe blog post, “Scaling ‘E-Waste’: LLMs on Multiple Decommissioned GPUs,” compares nine different builds — one to three K80s, P100s, or V100-16GB cards — on a single Supermicro dual-Xeon board. The test uses llama.cpp and covers more than 130 LLM tests, including Qwen 2.5, Gemma 4, and, of course, Qwen 3.6, at Q4/Q8/F16 precisions and from 4K to 128K context sizes. GPU energy per run is also recorded. The builder is “daily driving Qwen 3.6 35B” on the V100s and notes that scaling decommissioned GPUs will only get you so far.“E-waste,” in this case, refers to decommissioned enterprise GPUs, which are a popular but somewhat underpowered option when compared to very expensive modern alternatives. The Nvidia Tesla V100s in question are tested as a follow-up to a July round which tested 15 “e-waste” GPUs, and this time the board and CPUs stay the same for every build — the Supermicro X10DRG-Q with two Intel Xeon E5-2687W 12-core CPUs, powered by the Corsair HX1500i PSU.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Performance is judged based on what is considered “realtime interaction” which, here, is 70 tokens per second. As to why the number of GPUs is three: Qwen 3.6 35B, the primary tested model, fails on just one or two at Q8, or 8-bit quantization.Here are the given prices, with the note that they aren’t “100% reflective of what you could find on eBay today,” although the totals count only one of the two CPUs and omit RAM, storage, the case, and any cooling. You may like Benchmarking Qwen 3.8 27B on RTX 5090 and beyond Going deep on local AI performance benchmarking with Apple’s Mac Studio with M5 Ultra taking on Nvidia DGX Spark Lawyer builds private AI server with eight used Nvidia V100 GPUs Swipe to scroll horizontally What the builder paid for each three-card build Part 3x K80 3x P100 3x V100-16GB Three GPUs $270 ($90 each) $403.50 ($134.50 each) $655.16 ($436.77 per pair) Board $211 $211 $211 PSU $147.70 $147.70 $147.70 One CPU $28.20 $28.20 $28.20 Builder’s total $657 $790 $1,042 With 2nd CPU $685 $819 $1,070 The older cards are relatively inexpensive because they “run hot and ship without cooling,” which required the builder to 3D print one blower duct per card and has led to the development of a standalone cooler.The bench itself involves 10 runs of 512 generated tokens per test with context pre-filled to 4K, 32K, 64K, or 128K. Qwen 3.6 35B is a mixture-of-experts (MoE) model, which only activates about 3 billion out of its 35 billion total parameters per token. The numbers that immediately follow are at Q8.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsorsThe token goal was easily reached…when the context window was small, or 4K. The 100.8 tokens per second there fell to 72.7 at 128K, still usable by the 70 tokens per second goal. The 27B model, which is not MoE, fared much worse, at 24.3 at 4K, 21.6 at 32K, 18.7 at 64K, and just 14.2 at 128K. The MoE ends up about four to five times faster, depending on the context size. Swipe to scroll horizontally Qwen 3.6 35B generation speed by context length (tokens per second) Setup 4K 32K 64K 128K 3x V100, Q8 100.8 89.4 83.5 72.7 2x V100, Q4 105.4 96.2 89.5 77.1 3x P100, Q8 55.2 50.9 47.5 40.2 M5 Max Mac, 8-bit 105.5 91.1 78.5 61.3 Also tested were other dense models of about 30B parameters. At 4K, Gemma 4 31B achieved 20.9 and Qwen 2.5 32B 21.0, while the MoE Gemma 4 26B cleared the 70 tokens per second bar with just two V100s at Q8. If you move down to Q4, or 4-bit quantization, two V100s can run Qwen 3.6 35B at 77.1 to 105.4 tokens per second, between 128K and 4K context size. This is where it’s claimed that adding more cards gives you more memory, which enables larger models to be run, but not speed. (Image credit: Tom's Hardware (data: esologic))The P100s, for comparison, only hit 40.2–55.2 tokens per second in the same context range with Q8 Qwen 3.6 35B, and the target 70 only with Qwen 2.5 3B. If we compare to more modern hardware — the Nvidia DGX Spark, MSRP $4,700, and the M5 Max Mac Studio, which starts at $2,499 but costs $5,399 with the tested 40-core GPU, 128GB of memory, and a 1TB SSD — the 3x V100 build holds its own, using sourced data. What to read next Reddit user pays $35 for a crypto mining rig left in a garage and gets 54GB of VRAM at 65 cents per GB Lawyer’s eight-V100 AI server moves DeepSeek from 2-bit to near-NVFP4 precision Hot Chips 2026: Nvidia presents Groq 3 LPX architecture and unveils its first third-party inference benchmark The Mac comparison comes from the oMLX benchmark page for the M5 Max with 40 GPU cores and 128GB of unified memory, and that hits 43.9 tokens per second with a ~195K-token prompt on the Qwen 3.6 35B model. The Mac is slightly ahead at 4K and 32K, while the V100s pull ahead at 64K and 128K, by 19% at the longest context. These numbers have to be taken loosely, as the machines use different runtimes.The Spark run came from Kleybrink’s dgx-spark-bench, using Ollama in thinking mode with short prompts. Its 45.8 tokens per second is less than half the V100s’ 4K figure.Going further to modern GPUs, which “destroy our decommissioned equivalents,” as the builder puts it, you get about 315 tokens per second on two H100s and about 455 on one B200 at 128K, the B200 roughly six times the V100 box, even though the hosted cards ran the full 16-bit model against the V100s’ 8-bit. Parasail, an inference provider, sponsored that comparison with dedicated H100 and B200 deployments.As for energy, the V100 setup came out to about 0.02 kWh for a 128K 35B run, with the P100s taking twice that much and two or three K80s as much as 0.35 to 0.45 kWh. The V100-16GB simply “[puts] up better scores while consuming less energy,” in comparison to the P100s. These numbers are for the GPUs and not from the wall.There’s more to come. The builder wants a benchmark that “maps to ‘software factory’ performance,” a term for models being prompted constantly, around the clock, where instant speed matters less. Then there’s the cooler, which is “almost ready for release,” with beta testers to be recruited from the mailing list, although no date has been given. From the Reddit thread, the builder mentions the intention to compare inference backends and use speculative decoding to improve performance. items.titleZh: Three 'e-waste' Nvidia V100s hit 100 tokens per second on Qwen 3.6 35B in a $1,042 homelab rig
items.descriptionZh:
一位 homelab（自建实验室）玩家用三块退役的 Nvidia Tesla V100-16GB 企业级 GPU，也就是所谓“电子垃圾”，搭建本地推理平台，在 Qwen 3.6 35B 上实现约 100 token/s（每秒 token 数），按作者口径整机成本约 1042 美元。这项测试来自博客《Scaling ‘E-Waste’: LLMs on Multiple Decommissioned GPUs》，是此前 15 块退役 GPU 测试的延续。平台统一采用 Supermicro X10DRG-Q 双路 Xeon E5-2687W 主板和 Corsair HX1500i 电源，比较 1 至 3 块 K80、P100、V100-16GB 共九种组合，使用 llama.cpp 跑了 130 多项 LLM 测试，覆盖 Qwen 2.5、Gemma 4、Qwen 3.6，以及 Q4/Q8/F16 精度和 4K 至 128K 上下文，并记录每次运行的 GPU 能耗。作者也提醒，价格并非当前 eBay 行情的完全复现，且 1042 美元只计一块 CPU，不含内存、存储、机箱和散热。老旧卡便宜，但发热大、出厂无散热器，作者需为每块卡 3D 打印鼓风机风道，并开发独立散热器。

性能测试以 70 token/s 作为“实时交互”门槛。Qwen 3.6 35B 是 MoE（专家混合）模型，每个 token 只激活约 35B 总参数中的 3B；在 Q8（8 位量化）下，3 块 V100 在 4K 上下文达到 100.8 token/s，32K 为 89.4、64K 为 83.5、128K 为 72.7，长上下文仍超过门槛。相比之下，非 MoE 的稠密模型 Qwen 3.6 27B 在同一平台仅 24.3、21.6、18.7、14.2 token/s（4K/32K/64K/128K），MoE 版本快约 4 至 5 倍，说明参数更少不一定更快，激活参数和模型架构更关键。Qwen 3.6 35B 在 Q8 下需要 3 块 V100，1 至 2 块会因显存不足无法运行；降到 Q4 后，2 块 V100 可在 128K 至 4K 下达到 77.1 至 105.4 token/s。对比 3 块 P100 在 Q8 下仅 55.2、50.9、47.5、40.2 token/s，70 token/s 目标只在 Qwen 2.5 3B 等小模型上实现。其他约 30B 稠密模型在 4K 下，Gemma 4 31B 约 20.9、Qwen 2.5 32B 约 21.0 token/s；MoE 的 Gemma 4 26B 用 2 块 V100 Q8 即可超过 70 token/s。作者指出，增加显卡主要增加显存、支持更大模型，并不能线性提升速度。

与现代硬件对比，3 块 V100 方案在部分场景接近甚至超过更贵设备。M5 Max Mac Studio 测试配置为 40 核 GPU、128GB 内存、1TB SSD，售价 5399 美元；oMLX 数据显示其在约 195K 提示下跑 Qwen 3.6 35B 约 43.9 token/s，4K/32K 略领先 V100，但 64K/128K 被 V100 反超，最长上下文 V100 高约 19%。DGX Spark（MSRP 4700 美元）在 Kleybrink 的 dgx-spark-bench、Ollama thinking 模式短提示下为 45.8 token/s，不到 V100 4K 成绩的一半。现代 H100/B200 则明显更强：128K 下双 H100 约 315 token/s，单 B200 约 455 token/s，B200 约为 V100 方案的 6 倍，而且跑的是 16-bit 全精度模型，V100 为 8-bit；该对比由推理服务商 Parasail 赞助。由于运行时和测试条件不同，这些数字只能粗略参考。

能耗方面，V100 方案跑一次 128K、35B 推理约耗 0.02 kWh（仅 GPU），P100 约两倍，2 至 3 块 K80 高达 0.35 至 0.45 kWh；V100 相比 P100 分数更好且更省电。总体来看，这类退役 GPU 堆叠方案适合预算敏感的自建实验室、本地长上下文推理、隐私/离线场景和实验平台，能以较低现金成本获得可用吞吐，但需要承担散热改装、功耗、噪音、可靠性、驱动与软件兼容以及工程时间成本；它不能替代现代 GPU 或云 API 的峰值性能和能效。作者后续计划做更贴近“软件工厂”持续提示场景的基准，比较不同推理后端并尝试投机解码，独立散热器也接近发布。

history.title: AI data center power demand will double by 2030 thanks to $4 trillion in spending, adding an entire Great Britain to energy strain
history.description: IEA's report says that power production and distribution is barely keeping up with the rapid growth of AI data centers.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Instagram Share this article 3 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter The AI data center build-out is pushing electricity grids across the globe, with many regions facing demand from projects that would exceed the current peak load that each system could support. According to the International Energy Agency’s (IEA) World Energy Outlook 2026 report, a total of 120GW of capacity is currently available across all types of data centers across the globe, with another 120GW expected to be completed by the end of the decade, 75% of which would be dedicated to artificial intelligence. Aside from that, it’s also tracking 93 large “AI factories” that are either under construction or being expanded via satellite imagery. It estimates that the capacity for these sites grew from under 2GW to 17GW in just two years, and that they’re expected to hit a total of 50GW upon completion, the equivalent of adding a second Great Britain to power demand.Go deeper with TH Premium: AI and data centers (Image credit: Microsoft)The data center cooling state of playThe custom AI ASIC state of play America’s AI chip rules keep changing — and the rest of the world is paying the priceGTC 2026: Ian Buck press Q&A transcript — VP of Hyperscale and HPC speaks out on shelving CPX and shipping LPU decode this yearDemand for data center CPUs has surged, and AI agents are responsibleThis massive power consumption is one of the reasons for the opposition against their construction in communities, with residents blaming them for increased utility prices. However, the IEA says that its analysis “does not yet show a clear relationship between growth in data center capacity and increases in electricity prices.” It noted that if a data center uses existing capacity and pays for its share of the cost, then it could potentially lead to lower utility bills for all customers. However, if the grid operator is required to upgrade its system to accommodate the large consumer, then it could also lead to increased monthly bills if the costs are spread across all users.Emissions are another issue that the IEA has raised. Renewable energy dominates data centers’ power purchase agreements at nearly 50%, but actual power generation puts coal- and natural-gas power sources closer to 60%. This is likely due to the need for reliability, with the latter kicking in when the former cannot deliver the power that the data center needs. Aside from that, a few projects are deploying their own power, like Elon Musk’s Colossus 2 in Southaven, Mississippi, with about 180GW planned or under construction in the U.S. So, even though renewable energy is growing to accommodate demand, it’s also expected that coal- and natural-gas emissions from data centers will rise by 70% by 2030.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Investments in AI data centers are expected to hit $32 trillion by 2050, putting the infrastructure spending for the industry larger than railways, electrification, and the internet, combined. Despite that, the IEA says the grid remains a significant bottleneck — renewable power plants take between one and five years to complete, which is around the same time that some massive data center projects take if they do not face an extended moratorium, while transmission works can take three to five times longer. This is probably one of the reasons why some AI hyperscalers are choosing to put jet engines on their sites instead, although these are also facing shortages, especially in turbine blades. history.titleZh: 得益于4万亿美元支出，AI数据中心电力需求到2030年将翻倍，给能源系统增添相当于整个英国的负担
history.descriptionZh:
国际能源署（IEA）《2026年世界能源展望》报告显示，全球AI数据中心的快速扩张正在给各国电网带来巨大压力，许多地区的拟建项目用电需求将超过现有电网峰值负荷能力。目前，全球各类数据中心合计可用容量约为120GW，预计到本十年末还将新增120GW，其中75%将专门用于人工智能。IEA还通过卫星图像跟踪了93个正在建设或扩建的大型“AI工厂”，估算这些站点的容量在短短两年内从不足2GW增长到17GW，全部建成后总容量预计达到50GW，相当于为电力需求再增加一个英国的用电量。

大规模用电也引发了社区反对，居民担心数据中心推高电价。不过，IEA表示，其分析“尚未显示数据中心容量增长与电价上涨之间存在明确关系”。报告指出，如果数据中心利用现有电网容量并承担相应成本，可能反而有助于降低所有用户的电费；但如果电网运营商需要升级系统来容纳这类大型用户，且升级成本分摊给所有用户，月度账单可能上升。

排放问题同样受到关注。数据显示，可再生能源在数据中心电力购买协议中占比接近50%，但实际发电来源中煤炭和天然气接近60%。这很可能是因为数据中心需要稳定可靠的电力供应，当可再生能源无法满足需求时，化石能源会补位。部分项目开始自建电源，例如马斯克位于密西西比州Southaven的Colossus 2；美国还有约180GW的项目处于规划或在建状态。尽管可再生能源装机在增长，IEA仍预计到2030年，数据中心带来的煤炭和天然气排放将增加70%。

投资方面，到2050年，AI数据中心相关投资预计将达到32万亿美元，使该行业的基础设施支出超过铁路、电气化和互联网建设的总和。但IEA认为，电网仍是关键瓶颈：可再生能源电厂建设需要1至5年，大型数据中心项目若不遭遇长期禁令也大约需要类似时间，而输电工程耗时可达前者的3至5倍。这也可能是一些AI超大规模厂商选择在站点部署喷气发动机的原因之一，但这类设备同样面临供应短缺，尤其是涡轮叶片。总体来看，AI数据中心扩张不仅是算力问题，也正在成为电力供应、电网升级、排放和基础设施投资之间的系统性挑战。

history.title: NVIDIA and Microsoft Expand Accelerated Computing From Azure to Windows PCs
history.description: NVIDIA and Microsoft are extending their full-stack collaboration to help organizations build, customize and deploy intelligent applications — from next-generation infrastructure on Azure to industrial systems and Windows PCs. At Microsoft Ignite, the companies are expanding access to Azure virtual machines powered by NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 systems, as well as adding customer availability to […]
history.content: NVIDIA and Microsoft are extending their full-stack collaboration to help organizations build, customize and deploy intelligent applications — from next-generation infrastructure on Azure to industrial systems and Windows PCs. At Microsoft Ignite, the companies are expanding access to Azure virtual machines powered by NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 systems, as well as adding customer availability to NVIDIA open models and customization capabilities through Microsoft Foundry, and new options for running AI at the edge, where businesses generate and use their data. Microsoft is also using NVIDIA technologies to accelerate its own models and services, including NVIDIA Dynamo inference software for post-training and NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs for Bing search models. NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 Running in Azure NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 systems are running in Azure data centers, providing infrastructure designed for demanding reasoning, agentic applications, and large-scale model training and inference. Microsoft and NVIDIA are also collaborating to extend confidential computing to bare-metal and rack-scale AI infrastructure. The work will help protect sensitive models and data while they are being processed, supporting organizations that need to work with proprietary or regulated information. NVIDIA Confidential Computing and attestation help customers verify the computing environment before releasing sensitive models, data or keys. As AI workloads span more interconnected accelerators, the companies are working to extend those protections across the AI factory infrastructure. To help data centers get more performance from available power, NVIDIA and Microsoft are also collaborating on power efficiency using NVIDIA MaxLPS. Azure’s Vera Rubin preview builds on NVIDIA and Microsoft’s codesign and performance optimization, underscored in the latest NVIDIA Blackwell-based MLPerf results. In MLPerf Training v6.1, Azure scaled to 10,240 NVIDIA GPUs with GB200 NVL72 systems on the DeepSeek-V3 model, the largest scale in the round. In MLPerf Inference v6.1, Azure’s NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 systems led cloud submissions on DeepSeek-R1 interactive throughput by over 10%, per Signal65. Helping Enterprises Customize and Deploy Open Models Enterprise AI agents need to reason through complex tasks, find relevant company information and understand business documents. NVIDIA and Microsoft are expanding the models and services available through Microsoft Foundry to help developers bring these capabilities into business applications. Microsoft’s serverless Programmed Training offering gives developers control over post-training workflows while Foundry manages the underlying infrastructure. Enterprises can focus on their business data, evaluating model responses and improving model behavior. Foundry Managed Compute adds support for deploying custom model weights, helping connect model customization with deployment through Microsoft’s managed services. EY used Programmed Training in Microsoft Foundry to adapt NVIDIA Nemotron open models for classifying corporate purchasing records, improving accuracy on its evaluation dataset by 55% and lowering cost by 15x compared with proprietary frontier models. The work demonstrates how enterprises can customize open models for specialized business tasks. The expanded NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 lineup on Foundry Managed Compute supports different requirements across enterprise applications. Nemotron 3.5 Super is designed for long-running agents working across coding, research and business workflows, while Lightning supports applications that need fast responses and tool use. Complementary models help agents find relevant information with Nemotron Embed and Rerank, extract structured information from documents with Nemotron Parse and detect harmful content with Nemotron Content Safety. Nemotron 3.5 Bolt — designed for high-throughput, low-latency reasoning — and Transcribe, for speech recognition, are coming soon. Bringing AI Closer to Enterprise Data NVIDIA and Microsoft are expanding deployment options beyond the cloud, helping organizations run models and agents closer to their data while maintaining control over their infrastructure and operations. Expanded support for Nemotron 3.5 in Foundry Local brings capabilities for reasoning, coding and tool-using agents to Azure Local environments. Retrieval models help applications find evidence across text, document images, charts and tables. Azure Local will also support NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs from hardware partners, giving organizations additional options for deploying AI on premises. Azure Local is expanding to NVIDIA Jetson Thor and Jetson Orin edge AI platforms to support industrial applications such as machine vision, robotics and autonomous operations. NVIDIA physical AI models, including Cosmos, are also being brought to Foundry Local. On Windows PCs powered by NVIDIA RTX Spark, NVIDIA and Microsoft will showcase local large language model experiences at Ignite, demonstrating how developers can run AI applications directly on devices. For organizations using Cloud PCs, the companies are bringing Direct Stream capabilities to GPU-accelerated Windows 365 Cloud PCs. These capabilities support demanding graphics applications with up to two 4K streams at 60 frames per second and low latency, even over challenging networks. A limited preview is open for sign-ups, with public preview planned for early 2027. Connecting Scientific AI With Microsoft Discovery For scientific research, NVIDIA BioNemo Agent Toolkit and NVIDIA ALCHEMI Toolkit are expanding into the Microsoft Discovery catalog, bringing models for life sciences, drug discovery and materials and chemical science into Microsoft’s agentic research platform. BioNeMo Agent Toolkit helps scientists use natural language to run computational biology workflows in Microsoft Discovery, with agents coordinating the tools and model calls needed to carry out the work. An initial integration uses the RFD4-Proteina model, developed in collaboration with the University of Washington’s Institute for Protein Design, to generate candidate protein structures and amino acid sequences for further evaluation and laboratory validation. Accelerating Microsoft’s Models and Services Alongside expanding customer access to NVIDIA technologies, Microsoft is using NVIDIA software and accelerated computing in its own AI development and services. Microsoft AI uses NVIDIA Dynamo to support reinforcement learning rollout inference during post-training. This computationally intensive process generates the experiences used to improve models. Dynamo coordinates inference across a large GPU fleet, optimizing performance, as well as helping manage requests, model updates and recovery from failures. The deployment builds on joint engineering between Microsoft AI and NVIDIA. Visit NVIDIA at Ignite for demonstrations spanning enterprise applications, robotics, accelerated data processing and local computing, with hardware including an NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 rack and RTX Spark devices. View NVIDIA sessions, hands-on labs and booth theater presentations.

history.titleZh: NVIDIA 与微软将加速计算从 Azure 扩展至 Windows PC
history.descriptionZh:
NVIDIA与Microsoft在Microsoft Ignite上宣布扩展全栈合作，目标是帮助企业在从Azure云端到工业系统、边缘设备和Windows PC的完整范围内构建、定制和部署智能应用。背景是企业AI正从试验走向生产，既需要更强的大规模推理、智能体应用和模型训练基础设施，也需要开放模型定制、敏感数据保护、能效优化以及更靠近数据源的边缘部署能力。双方此次合作覆盖AI工厂基础设施、Microsoft Foundry模型定制与部署、边缘AI、科学发现以及微软自身模型和服务加速。

在云端基础设施方面，NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72系统已在Azure数据中心运行，面向高要求的推理、智能体应用以及大规模模型训练和推理。Azure的Vera Rubin预览建立在NVIDIA与Microsoft协同设计和性能优化基础上。双方还将机密计算扩展到裸金属和机架级AI基础设施，帮助保护处理过程中的敏感模型和数据，并通过NVIDIA机密计算与认证机制，在释放敏感模型、数据或密钥前验证计算环境；随着AI工作负载跨越多互联加速器，相关保护也将扩展到AI工厂基础设施。为提升数据中心在可用电力下的性能，双方还基于NVIDIA MaxLPS合作优化能效。性能对比方面，最新Blackwell平台MLPerf结果提供了参考：在MLPerf Training v6.1中，Azure使用GB200 NVL72系统将DeepSeek-V3训练扩展到10,240块NVIDIA GPU，为本轮最大规模；在MLPerf Inference v6.1中，据Signal65，Azure的NVIDIA GB300 NVL72系统在DeepSeek-R1交互吞吐上领先云提交超过10%。

在开放模型与企业定制方面，双方通过Microsoft Foundry扩大模型和服务可用性。Microsoft的无服务器Programmed Training让开发者控制后训练工作流，而Foundry管理底层基础设施，使企业可聚焦业务数据、评估模型响应并改进模型行为；Foundry Managed Compute新增对部署自定义模型权重的支持，把模型定制与通过微软托管服务部署连接起来。EY使用Microsoft Foundry中的Programmed Training适配NVIDIA Nemotron开放模型，对企业采购记录进行分类，在评估数据集上准确率提升55%，成本降至专有前沿模型的1/15（降低15倍），展示了企业针对专门业务任务定制开放模型的可行性。扩展的NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5阵容覆盖不同企业应用需求：Nemotron 3.5 Super面向跨编码、研究和业务工作流的长时运行智能体，Lightning面向需要快速响应和工具使用的应用；Nemotron Embed和Rerank帮助智能体检索相关信息，Nemotron Parse从文档中提取结构化信息，Nemotron Content Safety检测有害内容；面向高吞吐、低延迟推理的Nemotron 3.5 Bolt和语音识别模型Transcribe即将推出。

在边缘和终端方面，双方把部署选项从云扩展到更靠近企业数据的位置，同时保持企业对基础设施和运营的控制。Foundry Local扩展支持Nemotron 3.5，将推理、编码和工具调用智能体能力带到Azure Local环境；检索模型可跨文本、文档图像、图表和表格寻找证据。Azure Local还将支持来自硬件合作伙伴的NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPU，为本地部署AI提供更多选择，并扩展到NVIDIA Jetson Thor和Jetson Orin边缘AI平台，支持机器视觉、机器人、自主运营等工业应用；包括Cosmos在内的NVIDIA物理AI模型也被引入Foundry Local。在搭载NVIDIA RTX Spark的Windows PC上，双方将在Ignite展示本地大语言模型体验，说明开发者可直接在设备上运行AI应用。对于使用云PC的组织，双方将Direct Stream能力引入GPU加速的Windows 365 Cloud PC，支持高要求图形应用以低延迟实现最多两路4K 60帧/秒流，即使网络条件具有挑战性；该能力已开放有限预览注册，计划于2027年初进入公共预览。

在科学AI方面，NVIDIA BioNeMo Agent Toolkit和NVIDIA ALCHEMI Toolkit正在进入Microsoft Discovery目录，把生命科学、药物发现以及材料与化学科学模型引入微软的智能体研究平台。BioNeMo Agent Toolkit帮助科学家用自然语言在Microsoft Discovery中运行计算生物学工作流，由智能体协调所需工具和模型调用；初始集成采用与华盛顿大学蛋白质设计研究所合作开发的RFD4-Proteina模型，生成候选蛋白质结构和氨基酸序列，供进一步评估和实验室验证。与此同时，Microsoft也在用NVIDIA技术加速自身模型和服务：Microsoft AI使用NVIDIA Dynamo支持后训练中的强化学习rollout推理，Dynamo在大规模GPU集群上协调推理、优化性能，并帮助管理请求、模型更新和故障恢复；Bing搜索模型则使用NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPU加速。整体来看，这一合作把云端AI工厂、开放模型定制、边缘与PC部署、科学发现和微软自身服务连接为全栈体系，使企业能够在Azure、本地和边缘环境中部署智能体应用，并在性能、成本、数据主权与合规之间取得平衡。

history.title: Into the Omniverse: How Developers Turn Ideas Into Simulations With Frontier AI Agents
